steps.content: By the time you return to the stele garden, the day is already bright.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: I've decided to terminate this collaboration.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: I'm not yet skillful enough to interpret a regret from that long ago. Perhaps letting it go would be best for all of us.
She looks at the old site of the mass grave not far away, which has long since been covered up. Oak Casket's gaze looks as if she's staring into an abyss.
You flip through the doctor's journal, a thin volume that's somewhat old. Luckily, it contains the information you're looking for.
It is what Oak Casket has missed over the years, what she still needs to see now.
...You told me about the legend of the falcon before, but you didn't finish.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: You turn out to be quite a talker, you know.
The pocket of wealth is found where merchants gathered and the pocket of power is found in war...
The pocket of hope lies in utter pain.
Because hope is most elusive to the living. It hides in the places the living are least likely to go near.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: You sure have many original ideas.
That stele... is related to you, isn't it?
Oak Casket says nothing and falls silent.
That stele's regret is all blurry now, but it has persisted for so long. I can only imagine how intense it originally was.
Why can't we persist a little longer for him too? Give it another try?
Isn't it your wish that all the deceased ones can leave this world without any regrets?
You spread the notes you found at the doctor's apartment and lay them out in front of the tombstone.
The handwriting on the notes has faded, some of the ink smudged due to moisture. Only the word light is still clear, as if someone has retraced it carefully.
You respect our contract. Our agreement hasn't reached an end yet.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: This is why I hate dealing with the living.
Oak Casket stands there quietly. Though a little hesitant, she doesn't stop you from getting near her.
You reach out to her slender body as cold as her words. You cover her eyes.
Incessant whispers echo in your ears, clinging to your nerves, bringing you pain.
Oak Casket seems to want to pull your hand away, but you hold hers instead.
It's okay, Oak Casket, I'm not afraid.
You hold her hand firmly until the temperatures of both hands gradually even out, becoming equally warm.
You begin to recognize the voices in your ears. Two old voices.

The moment you recognize them, the power of the shackles becomes more intense than ever, and your vision has never been more clear. There is light in front of you, and it keeps brightening until you can see everything clearly.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Why is light always granted to those with an uneasy journey? Why is life always granted to those with a bitter soul...
Oak Casket's voice trembles slightly.
The moon shines upon the stele. The little girl sits under the wooden board, reciting the poem she's copied by the moonlight.
When she looks up at the person approaching her, you finally make out her face. It's a young Oak Casket.

steps.speaker: Old Priest
steps.content: What are you doing here, Nona?

steps.speaker: Young Oak Casket
steps.content: I'm reading the poem you taught me today, Father. But there are many words I don't know.

steps.speaker: Old Priest
steps.content: Let me see.

steps.speaker: Old Priest
steps.content: The golden falcon... Oh, that bird is the sun's companion. Do you remember that funerals are usually held before dawn?

steps.speaker: Young Oak Casket
steps.content: I remember.

steps.speaker: Old Priest
steps.content: The dead live in a different world than the living. But when the falcon arrives, it means the sun is rising.

steps.speaker: Old Priest
steps.content: Let's read it together.

steps.speaker: Old Priest & Young Oak Casket
steps.content: The wanderer in the wilderness no longer carried the burden of the past. The golden falcon asked her: Where came you? She said: I do not recall the way I came. Dawn is near, as is the end of everything.

You see the light getting brighter. In that white light, a younger doctor appears, along with some people from the monastery. They gather around the young Oak Casket, reciting the unfinished poem together, as if completing a devout worship.

steps.speaker: Crowd
steps.content: You shall endure hardships and surpass all stelae in this world. You shall meet the golden falcon, and the winged traveler will guide you to the light. Where there is light, there you shall be.
The pages turn. The fire colors the full moon red.
The gangsters' roars and gunfire end the quiet world.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: Father, Nona is not dead. There's still hope for her...

steps.speaker: Old Priest
steps.content: Her injuries are grave. With our current supplies and equipment, we can't save her...

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: But she's not dead yet! She's looking at us from the bottom of the pit! Maybe she can survive this...

steps.speaker: Old Priest
steps.content: Those scoundrels are coming soon! They've finally found an excuse to attack the monastery, and they will surely take Nona away, dead or alive! Don't you know what they're going to do to her?!

steps.speaker: Old Priest
steps.content: Instead of being infected with Mania in those experiments... it's better... to surrender her to hope...

steps.speaker: Old Priest
steps.content: The blessing has long abandoned us... but still, I wish... she could see hope... see the light...
The pages turn again.
The doctor sat in front of the stele, which looked less dilapidated than it is now.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: Nona... Father... did you meet again in the afterlife?

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: Give him a beating. Stay mad at him. He was still repenting to you until his last breath.
The doctor seemed to be remembering something, his eyes reddening again. Finally, he sighed.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: I'm the only one left in the monastery. I'll come to pray for you both often, until the day I can't anymore.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: You must go where there is light.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: You shall endure hardships and surpass all stelae in this world. You shall meet the golden falcon, and the winged traveler will guide you to the light. Where there is light, there you shall be.
Countless praying rituals flash before your eyes. The young doctor turns into a middle-aged one, then into an old man. In the end, only the unvisited grave is left.
As all the chants blend into a unison, the regrets intensify, until the vast light reaches its limit.
Slowly, the light goes out.
You remove your hands covering Oak Casket's eyes.
Nona.
Oak Casket nods. There is a gleam of resignation and indulgence in her eyes.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: This was the name the priest gave me, as I was adopted on the ninth day of that month. But Nona is dead.
Her hand gently traces the inscriptions on the stele. You can now vaguely make out a number that had been scratched out. It's the number nine.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: You guessed right. This is Nona's stele.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: I suppose this is the cenotaph they erected for me after they threw me into that mass grave.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: I used to think... that this cenotaph was like an elegy they recited for me... that it was nothing more than an excuse to absolve them of their guilt...
No, they...
Oak Casket interrupts you.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: I'll settle this once and for all.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: But I need some time...
You look at Oak Casket, whose eyes have regained their usual tranquility.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Go back to the Bureau first. There are things I must tend to here. Please rest assured. I won't go anywhere before I've fulfilled our agreement.
Three days later, you receive an invitation in black.

Dear friend, you are cordially invited to preside over the funeral of a nameless one. May her tears stop now and her suffering end here. The funeral will be held at the Romanesque stele garden at the following time and date.
The invitation is plainly decorated and bears no signature. Nevertheless, you decide to attend the ceremony.

You arrive at the stele garden. As expected, there are no other participants. You walk up to the small podium, read the opening lines at the time stipulated on the invitation, and then make the speeches according to the agenda.
The atmosphere is somewhat bizarre, as the only audience are those stelae of different sizes.

Greetings, dear friends. I know it's strange to say this because you can't even respond to me. Or perhaps you hear my words, but I can't understand your secret language. But I know there is someone here who can understand you.

The world is populated with living beings. This hasn't changed even after Nightfall. One day, I came to the sudden realization that even though the dead outnumber the living, we have never paid attention to the voices of the dead.
I want to thank a friend who made me realize this.
The wind stirs the forest, sounding like the revenants' whispers. You think you hear Oak Casket's chuckle.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: The living believe their prayers can cleanse the souls of the dead, helping them find relief. They cover up their sins with such grandiose rhetoric, as if they can earn forgiveness from the dead just like that.
The dead need not answer the living's confessions, for the path and the past both belong to the dead themselves.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: What's the point? He threw me into the darkness, but told me to find the light.
The dead need not bear the blessings of the living, for the dead can reach the gate of life with their own strength.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Does the pocket of hope exist in this world?
A world without hope is the collective sin of the living. I will cover her eyes until a new world replaces the old one.
Your gaze sweeps across the undulating stelae, finally landing on one that's already been repaired.
This is your answer to all of Oak Casket's questions. You believe she's hearing it.
Last but not least, I would like to recite a poem, one she knows by heart.

The wanderer in the wilderness no longer carried the burden of the past. The golden falcon asked her: Where came you? She said: I do not recall the way I came. Dawn is near, as is the end of everything.
You shall endure hardships and surpass all stelae in this world. You shall meet the golden falcon, and the winged traveler will guide you to the light. Where there is light, there you shall be.
You understand Oak Casket's intention. She held a funeral for her younger self to bid her bitter past farewell.
After the funeral is done, you walk to the repaired stele. An open casket made of oak lies there.
Now that the little girl named Nona has been laid to rest, I have a question for the messenger of the dead. Sinner Oak Casket, why do you continue to linger in this mortal world?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: The day I was saved by the dead, I gained my power, so I chose to become a messenger for them, serving those lingering between life and death. Yet there was one thing I never understood: What kept them lingering in this world?
And has she figured it out now?

The cover of the casket is left open. You suddenly realize the casket is made of fresh oak wood. Oak Casket must have collected the trunk of that blasted oak tree, as there are burn marks on the wood.
This is a real Oak Casket.
Oak Casket's voice comes from the shadow inside the casket.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: No. But maybe you can help her figure it out.
You reach out to Oak Casket. Gently, she takes your hand and stands up from her casket.
The oak tree was felled by the explosion and will never sprout again. But the seeds of hope will.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Thank you for seeing Nona off.
If you really mean it, maybe stop chasing after me with the coffin you've made for me?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: I won't urge you to come back to my side so soon before we see a new world.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: I've always wondered why I stay in the world of the living...

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: But your existence may help me find the meaning.
